en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fourth Chapter
The Discourse on Possession of Equanimity:
Is an Arahant possessed of six kinds of equanimity?
Is it to be said that an Arahant is endowed with six types of contact, six types of feeling, six types of perception... [and so on] ...six types of wisdom?
No, it should not be said thus... [and so on]....
Is it to be said that an Arahant is endowed with six types of equanimity?

“Then does an arahant, while seeing a form with the eye, hear a sound with the ear, smell an odor with the nose, taste a flavor with the tongue, touch a tangible object with the body, and cognize a mental phenomenon with the mind;

and conversely, while cognizing a mental phenomenon with the mind, see a form with the eye, hear a sound with the ear, smell an odor with the nose, taste a flavor with the tongue, and touch a tangible object with the body?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is an Arahant possessed of six kinds of equanimity? Yes.
“Is it not the case that one who is constantly, continuously, and uninterruptedly endowed with the six equanimities is concentrated, and that the six equanimities are established?
One should not say so… [as before]… One should not say so.
“Is an arahant endowed with six kinds of equanimity?”—
Yes. Is it not the case that an arahant possesses the sixfold equanimity?
“If an Arahant possesses the sixfold equanimity, then indeed it must be said:
‘An Arahant is endowed with six kinds of equanimity’ … [and so on] …”
The Discussion on Being Endowed with Equanimity is finished.
